711241.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hréwō, from Proto-Indo-European *sréweti, from *srew- (“to flow; to stream”). Cognates include Sanskrit स्रव॑ति (srávati), Old Church Slavonic строуꙗ (struja, “stream”).

711243.t: Uncertain. Probably from Proto-Indo-European *wreh₁ǵ- (“to break”); compare Old Armenian երգիծանեմ (ergicanem, “to tear, dissect”), Lithuanian rėžti, and Old Church Slavonic рѣзати (rězati, “to cut, slaughter”).

711208.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew רָחֵל (rāḥēl), from Proto-Semitic *raḫil-.

711282.t: Three possibilities are: * Pre-Greek name - see Phoenician 𐤄𐤓𐤏𐤃 (hrʿd, “snake”), a reference to the serpents that had supposedly inhabited the land in ancient times. * From ῥόα (rhóa, “pomegranate”). * From ῥόδον (rhódon, “rose”).

711228.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *wer- Proto-Indo-European *werb- Proto-Indo-European *wremb-der.? Pre-Greekder.? Proto-Indo-European *wergʷ- Proto-Indo-European *wrengʷ-der.? Ancient Greek ῥέμβω Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *wremb-,…

711281.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wródon, borrowed from some Eastern language, most likely Proto-Iranian *wardah (“flower, rose”) (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀺𐀈𐀸 (wo-do-we), Old Persian *vr̥dah, Aramaic 𐡅𐡀𐡓𐡃𐡀 (warda), Classical Syriac ܘܪܕܐ (wardā), Old Armenian վարդ…

711240.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ser-? Proto-Indo-European *srew- Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥? Proto-Hellenic *hréumə Ancient Greek ῥεῦμα From Proto-Hellenic *hréumə, likely inherited from Proto-Indo-European *sréwmn̥, from…

711252.t: The suffixes -ινος (-īnos) and -ινη (-īnē) are found both with inherited and with Pre-Greek substrate words. Since there are no good cognates, however, the word is probably Pre-Greek.

711209.t: According to Beekes of Pre-Greek origin or related to Lithuanian ražis (“stubble”). Compare ῥαχός (rhakhós, “thorn hedge”).

711291.t: Borrowed from Thracian, ultimately possibly from Proto-Indo-European *Hrewp- (“to break”), likely closely related to Albanian rrufé (“lightning”).

711273.t: Perhaps related to ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”), because of the richness of the juice, with hypothetical original form *ῥοϝ-ιά (*rhow-iá). However, a Pre-Greek origin remains a serious option for this word.

711293.t: Traditionally derived from ῥέπω (rhépō, “to decline, descend”), but perhaps not related to the verb.

711259.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sríHgos and cognate with Latin frīgus (“cold, frost”).

711286.t: According to Beekes, if related to ῥοῖβδος (rhoîbdos, “buzzing, hissing noise”), this word is certainly of Pre-Greek origin, but even if unrelated, such an origin may still be considered.

711253.t: From Proto-Indo-European *wr̥h₁tós, from *werh₁- (“to speak, say”). Equivalent to εἴρω (eírō, “I say”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

711250.t: From the stem ῥη- (rhē-) of εἴρω (eírō, “to say”) + -σις (-sis, abstract noun suffix).

711262.t: From ῥιζόω (rhizóō) + -μα (-ma). See Ancient Greek ῥίζα (rhĭ́ză).
